functions.name: InflateDecompress
functions.summary: Outer DEFLATE inflate state machine (zlib-style): parses block headers (stored / fixed-Huffman / dynamic-Huffman), reads the dynamic-block code-length tables, builds the Huffman decode tables, drives the literal/length decode loop, and flushes the circular output window. Operates on an inflate-context object a1 (state field this+0x0, remaining-length this+0x4, loop counter this+0x8, work/table buffer this+0xC, decode bit count this+0x10, decode table this+0x14, bfinal flag this+0x18, bit count this+0x1C, bit accumulator this+0x20, max code length this+0x24, window bounds this+0x28/0x2C, window capacity this+0x30, output cursor this+0x34) and a stream object a2 (input pointer a2[0], input remaining a2[1], consumed counter a2[2], error-string slot a2[6], allocator/deallocator fn ptrs a2[8]/a2[9], owner a2[10]). Returns 1 on stream end, the sub_52A5D7 flush result when more input is needed, -2 on an invalid state, -3 on data/bitstream errors, -4 on table allocation failure. Called by sub_517ADC (InflateBlockProcessor).

operations.description: Entry/loop guard: if the state field (this+0x0) exceeds 9 the state is invalid; set return code -2 and jump to the state-persist/return path (LABEL_5).

Snapshot stream state into locals on entry: input read pointer v7 = *a2, remaining input v82 = a2[1], bit accumulator v83 = this+0x20, bit count v84 = this+0x1C, output cursor v81 = this+0x34; compute available output-window space v80 from the window-end this+0x2C, window capacity this+0x30 and cursor.

Infinite state-machine loop: dispatch on the state selector (this+0x0) through the jump table jpt_5277CE (0x00527EC5); after each case, reload the state from this+0x0, restore the stream/pointer locals and continue until a return.

case 0 (block header): top up the bit buffer to 3 bits from the input, then read bfinal = this+0x18 = v83 & 1 and block type = (v83 & 7) >> 1. Type 0 (stored): align bits and set state 1. Type 1 (fixed): consume 3 bits and build the fixed-Huffman tables. Type 2 (dynamic): consume 3 bits and set state 3. Type 3: invalid.

case 0 fixed-Huffman path: call ArithmeticComparison_a5a8 with four by-ref stack outputs to derive the fixed literal/length and distance table parameters, then call FieldSetterWithVTableAlloc to allocate the fixed decode tables; store the resulting table into this+0x4 and transition to state 6 (decode). If the allocation returns null, jump to the -4 memory-failure path.

case 0 invalid block type: set the state to 9 (error), write the invalid-block-type error string (aInvalidBlockTy) into the stream error slot a2[6], persist bit state and go to the error return path (return -3).

case 1 (stored block header): top up to 16 bits and read LEN = this+0x4 = (u16)v83; guard `~v83 >> 16 != (u16)v83` (NLEN complement check); on mismatch set state 9, write the invalid-stored-block-lengths error string (aInvalidStoredB) into a2[6] and return -3. On match clear the bit state.

case 1 end-of-header transition: if the stored length (this+0x4) is zero (guard:1) finish the block immediately, selecting the next state from bfinal: state 7 when this+0x18 != 0 (guard:3, final block) or state 0 when this+0x18 == 0 (guard:4, more blocks); otherwise enter state 2 (stored copy).

case 2 (stored copy): copy up to min(this+0x4 remaining length, remaining input, available window space v80) bytes from the input pointer to the output window via qmemcpy; advance the read pointer, cursor, input counter and v80; decrement this+0x4. When the length reaches zero (guard:1) end the block (bfinal ? state 7 : state 0).

case 2 window-full flush: when v80 (window space) reaches zero, persist the output cursor into this+0x34 and call sub_52A5D7 to flush/refill the output window; on refill recompute the window bounds from this+0x28/0x2C/0x30 and re-derive v80; if the window cannot be refilled, persist bit state, input counters and cursor, then return the sub_52A5D7 result.

case 3 (dynamic block header): top up to 14 bits and read HLIT = v83 & 0x1F, HDIST = (v83 >> 5) & 0x1F and HCLEN = v83 >> 10 into this+0x4 (14-bit combined field). Guard: if HLIT or HDIST exceeds 0x1D, set state 9 and write the too-many-length-or-distance-symbols error string (aTooManyLengthO) into a2[6] (return -3).

case 3 table allocation: allocate the code-length work table by calling the stream allocator a2[8](a2[10], HDIST + HLIT + 258, 4); store the pointer into this+0xC; if null, jump to the -4 memory-failure path. Consume the 14 header bits, clear this+0x8 and set state 4.

case 4 (read code-length code lengths): loop while this+0x8 < (HCLEN + 4) and while this+0x8 < 0x13 (guard:2): read a 3-bit code length into this+0xC + 4 * dword_5B06E8[this+0x8], where dword_5B06E8 is the fixed HCLEN order permutation table; increment this+0x8; afterwards zero-fill the remaining entries up to 0x13. Topping up the bit buffer may hit the need-more-input path.

case 4 build code-length tree: set this+0x10 (bit count) to 7, then call sub_52A426(this+0xC, &this+0x10, &this+0x14, this+0x24, a2) to build the code-length Huffman decode table at this+0x14 using the max-code-length parameter this+0x24; on a nonzero return free this+0xC via the deallocator a2[9] and jump to the error path (state 9 / -3).

case 5 (read literal/length and distance code lengths): loop this+0x8 up to (HDIST + HLIT + 258). Decode each symbol from this+0x14 by indexing `this+0x14 + 8 * (v83 & dword_5DA520[this+0x10])` with the bit mask table dword_5DA520, reading the code bit length from table+1 and the symbol value from table+4. Values below 0x10 are stored directly into this+0xC; repeat codes 16/17/18 consume their extra bits and replicate the previous length or a run of zeros. Guard: if the run overruns the (HDIST + HLIT + 258) budget, free this+0xC and write the invalid-bit-length-repeat error string (aInvalidBitLeng) into a2[6], then return -3.

On success call FieldSetterWithVTableAlloc with the computed table parameters and store the tree into this+0x4; a null allocation jumps to the -4 path; then set state 6.

case 6 (decode literals/lengths): persist the bit state (this+0x1C/0x20), input counters and cursor, then call sub_529B2C (the inner literal/length+distance decode state machine); if its result is not 1, return sub_52A5D7(a1, a2, a3). Otherwise call IndirectCallDispatch(this+0x4, a2) to run the decode trees, reload the stream state from a2, recompute the window space, and select the next state: 0 when bfinal (this+0x18) is 0 (guard:4) or 7 when it is set (guard:3).

case 7 (end of block): persist the cursor to this+0x34 and call sub_52A5D7 to flush the window; if the window capacity (this+0x30) is consumed, set state 8 and return 1; otherwise persist bit state, counters and cursor and return the sub_52A5D7 result.
case 8 (done): return 1 to signal complete decompression of the input stream.

case 9 / error return path (LABEL_110/LABEL_6): persist the bit accumulator into this+0x20, the bit count into this+0x1C, and the remaining input count into a2[1], then return -3 for data errors or -4 for the allocation-failure path (LABEL_120).

functions.summary: Applies a frequency-domain FIR-like convolution plus lookup-table decode to audio channel data and writes the interleaved result out. Returns the buffer pointer after both loops.

Per-channel guard: when *v8 or v8[-16] or v8[16] or v8[32] is nonzero the full convolution path runs, otherwise a scaled-passthrough path is taken.
Write the lowpass-ish sum result: *v23 = (v14 + v13 + 4096) >> 13.
Compute the highpass-ish difference v12 = (v13 - v14 + 4096) >> 13 (or, on the passthrough path, v12 = 4 * v11 * v10 and *v7 = v12), then store the second tap v7[8] = v12.

Decode the first output byte: *v16 = byte at (((v20 + v19 + 0x80000) >> 20) & 0x3FF) + v22 from the wave table; on the passthrough path *v16 = byte at (((v17 + 16) >> 5) & 0x3FF) + v6.

Advance result by 32 bytes, increment v25, and repeat while v25 < 2 for the two interleaved output samples.
Return result (the advanced v21 buffer pointer) after both loops complete.
